To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have used the extended l-summing Wong formula in semiclassical formalism to fit sub-barrier fusion data, and found that the barrier lowering and narrowing effects are not universal for different Skyrme force parameters.

the barrier modification in l-summed expression of Wong formula is sensitive to the Skyrme force used in the semiclassical formalism, and the Wong formula with SIII force fits the fusion-evaporative cross sections for 58,64 Ni + 58,64,100,108,112,116,120,124,128,132,136Mo reactions.

the Wong formula with Skrme forces in semiclassical ETF formalism fits the fusion-evaporated data of 64Ni+64Mo reaction exactly for GSkI force, but not for SIII and SV forces, requiring additional barrier modification for a best fit.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for a given nuclear reaction, the Wong formula with SEDF and ETF approach, with a proper Skyrme force, gives the best fit to the fusion-evaporation data without any extra barrier modification.
, for a given system, we could choose the proper Skyrme force, which gives proper barriers and fits the experimental data without any additional modifications.

The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the Wong formalism, the use of semiclassical ETF approach for the proximity potential with Skyrme force gives the barrier characteristics, which are in agreement with the experimental fusion-evaporation cross sections for the same reaction.
one can use the semiclassical ETF method with Skyrme force to fit the data without any additional barrier modifications, if a Skyrme energy functional is chosen properly.

, in order to obtain a best fit to fusion-evaporation cross sections, we do not need to modify barrier heights or widths, but we can use a Skyrme energy force which provides us with a barrier of proper characteristics.
